meta.analyst_notes: EYP-1901 delivers vorolanib (pan-VEGF TKI) via Durasert sustained-release intravitreal insert, targeting ~6-month dosing intervals in wet AMD. Current standard of care (Eylea, Vabysmo) requires injections every 4-16 weeks; real-world adherence is poor, with ~40% of patients undertreated at 12 months. Phase 2 DAVIO 2 showed 67% of patients maintained 6-month dosing through 9 months with BCVA gains comparable to aflibercept monthly injections. Key mispricing: the market prices this as a "me-too anti-VEGF" when the injection burden reduction is the main unmet need in wet AMD — adherence, not efficacy, is the limiting factor in real-world outcomes. ACUITY Phase 3 is powered for non-inferiority; success would unlock a large and durable market position given the dosing advantage.

asset.name: EYP-1901 (vorolanib)
asset.mechanism_of_action: Pan-VEGF tyrosine kinase inhibitor (vorolanib) formulated in Durasert sustained-release intravitreal insert. Delivers continuous low-level VEGF suppression from a single intravitreal injection lasting approximately 6 months, compared to monthly or quarterly injections required for current anti-VEGF biologics (Eylea, Vabysmo, Lucentis).

company.notes: Cash runway: ~195/22 ≈ 9 quarters. Sufficient to reach ACUITY readout. EyePoint raised $100M in equity in 2023 specifically to fund ACUITY through readout. No debt. Non-dilutive revenue from Dexycu/Yutiq legacy products (~$8M/quarter).

trials.primary_endpoint: Non-inferiority BCVA change from baseline (NI margin -4 letters) at 52 weeks
trials.notes: ACUITY is a 3-arm trial: EYP-1901 q6m, aflibercept q8w (active control), EYP-1901 PRN. Non-inferiority design reduces bar vs. superiority; BCVA is well-validated for FDA. Phase 2 DAVIO 2 showed +6.4 BCVA letters at 9 months (afl arm: +7.0); NI demonstrated. Main risk: deliver sustained drug levels at 6 months in all patients (tail of distribution).
Likely priority review given unmet need (injection burden) and strong Phase 2 data. Precedent: Susvimo (port delivery system) received PDUFA within 6 months of NDA.

what_would_change_thesis: ACUITY week-52 topline: BCVA NI demonstrated with ≥65% of patients at 6-month dosing → validates delivery + efficacy simultaneously (strong bull case).
ACUITY fails NI: primary endpoint missed → thesis ends; stock likely falls 70-80%.
FDA grants priority review for NDA → signals 'breakthrough-like' unmet need recognition; re-rates near-term.
Payer framework announcement pre-launch: if a major PBM pre-approves formulary positioning at semi-annual dosing premium → accelerates adoption trajectory.
Susvimo (Genentech) reports strong real-world 6-month durability data → validates semi-annual dosing as category; pulls EYP-1901 along.
Partnership or acquisition by Novartis/Roche/AbbVie → likely at significant premium to NAV given platform value of Durasert technology.
